Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Health | National Pru-East MP links recurring typhoid cases to broken water system, calls for urgent rehabilitation Source : Myjoyonline.com 19 November 2026 7:13pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Member of Parliament for Pru-East, Emmanuel Kwaku Boam, has told Parliament that typhoid is ravaging communities in his constituency due to lack of access to potable water.
He said the situation has escalated to cases of intestinal perforation, the acutest form of typhoid, which he described as a very big deal for the area.
Mr Boam raised the alarm when he asked the Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources about the state of the request for water supply intervention for the Parambo-Sawaba community, which had been submitted to the Community Water and Sanitation Agency (CWSA).
He said the crisis is not limited to Parambo-Sawaba alone, but affects about 99 communities in the Pru-East area, with residents forced to rely on unsafe water sources.
According to him, the affected enclave has a population of close to 50,000 people, while the wider catchment is estimated at over 500,000.
He said the health emergency, which dates back to 2022/2023, has persisted for years, with residents suffering repeated bouts of typhoid linked to the water they drink.
Mr Boam said although other interventions are ongoing, the core problem remains the water table and hard water in the area, and the rehabilitation of the water systems remains the only sustainable way to stop the infections.
Responding, the Minister admitted that the Parambo-Sawaba Water System is currently non-functional.
He said the CWSA is undertaking a comprehensive technical evaluation of the facility as part of an ongoing nationwide assessment of ninety-eight (98) broken-down water systems to determine the scope of rehabilitation works required.
He assured the House that upon completion of the assessment, the CWSA intends to prioritise the Parambo-Sawaba system for rehabilitation and include it among the first batch of facilities to be considered for reconstruction.
He added that the Ministry has been informed of a possible financial intervention from a financial institution through the Pru East District Assembly, and that the assessment results together with a priced Bill of Quantities will be shared with the Assembly to facilitate timely rehabilitation.
Mr Boam, however, insisted that with typhoid and intestinal perforation already taking a toll, the intervention cannot wait any longer.
